title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 103
paragraphs: Xerxes was greatly pleased with this advice, since she had succeeded in saying the very thing he himself was meaning to do — for not even if all the men and women in the world had counseled him to remain would he have done so, I think, so thoroughly had he been struck with terror. He commended Artemisia, then, and sent her away to escort his sons to Ephesus, since certain illegitimate sons of his were traveling with him.
